ap_computer_science_a-f04.title: LimitedCounter: design a class

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the complete LimitedCounter class, including the constructor and any required instance variables and methods. A LimitedCounter accepts increments until a limit that is given to the constructor is reached. increment adds one to the counter and returns true if the limit has not been reached, and returns false (without changing the counter) otherwise. reset sets the counter back to its starting value. remaining returns the number of increments still allowed. Examples of the behavior are listed in the following table.

| Statement | Result |
|---|---|
| LimitedCounter c = new LimitedCounter(5); | creates a counter that accepts at most 5 increments |
| c.increment() (called 5 times) | true each time |
| c.increment() | false (the limit has been reached) |
| c.remaining() | 0 |
| c.reset(); c.remaining() | 5 |

rubric_rows.criterion: Declares the class header public class LimitedCounter
Declares private instance variables that store the limit and the current progress
Constructor has the correct signature and records the limit (distinguishing parameter from field)
increment refuses the update once the limit is reached (boundary correct: at most the limit)
common_errors: uses <= so one extra is accepted

rubric_rows.criterion: increment updates the counter only when the increment is accepted
increment returns true when accepted and false when refused (return type boolean)
reset restores the starting state (void method)
remaining returns the number of increments still allowed (int method)
The class compiles as a whole with correct return types and public methods

ap_computer_science_a-f05.title: Scoreboard: design a class

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the complete Scoreboard class, including the constructor and any required instance variables and methods. A Scoreboard keeps the points of a home team and an away team in a game that ends when a team reaches a target number of points. The constructor takes the target. scoreHome and scoreAway add points to a team. leader returns "home" if the home team has more points, "away" if the away team has more points and "tie" if the scores are equal. isOver returns true if at least one team has reached the target. Examples of the behavior are listed in the following table.

| Statement | Value returned | Explanation |
|---|---|---|
| Scoreboard s = new Scoreboard(21); | (none) | A game that ends when a team reaches 21 points |
| s.scoreHome(4); | (none) | The home team has 4 points |
| s.scoreAway(4); | (none) | The away team has 4 points |
| s.leader() | "tie" | The scores are equal |
| s.scoreAway(17); | (none) | The away team now has 21 points |
| s.isOver() | true | A team has reached the target |
| s.leader() | "away" | The away team has more points |

rubric_rows.criterion: Declares the class header public class Scoreboard
Declares private instance variables that store the target and both scores
Constructor has the correct signature, stores the target and starts both scores at 0 (distinguishing parameter from field)
scoreHome adds the points to the home score (accumulates, void method)
scoreAway adds the points to the away score only
leader returns the String "home" or "away" for the team with more points
leader returns "tie" when the scores are equal (the cases do not overlap)
isOver returns true when either team has reached the target (at least, with a logical or)
All methods have the correct headers and return types (void, String, boolean) and the class compiles as a whole

ap_computer_science_a-f06.title: Stock: design a class

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Write the complete Stock class, including the constructor and any required instance variables and methods. A Stock records the name of an item and the quantity of it in stock. The constructor takes the name and the starting quantity. getName and getQuantity return them. restock adds units to the quantity. sell removes units and returns true if there is enough stock; otherwise it returns false and leaves the quantity unchanged. Examples of the behavior are listed in the following table.

| Statement | Value returned | Explanation |
|---|---|---|
| Stock s = new Stock("mugs", 5); | (none) | A stock of 5 mugs |
| s.sell(3) | true | There was enough stock; 2 remain |
| s.sell(4) | false | Not enough stock; the quantity does not change |
| s.restock(10); | (none) | The quantity becomes 12 |
| s.sell(12) | true | All of the stock is sold |
| s.getQuantity() | 0 | Nothing remains |
| s.getName() | "mugs" | The name given to the constructor |
